paragraphs.text: And when they drew nigh unto Jerusalem, and came unto Bethphage, unto the mount of Olives, then Jesus sent two disciples,
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ὅτε ἤγγισαν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα καὶ ἦλθον εἰς Βηθφαγὴ εἰς τὸ Ὄρος τῶν Ἐλαιῶν, τότε Ἰησοῦς ἀπέστειλεν δύο μαθητὰς
paragraphs.translit: Kai hote ēngisan eis Hierosolyma kai ēlthon eis Bēthphagē eis to Oros tōn Elaiōn, tote Iēsous apesteilen dyo mathētas

paragraphs.text: saying unto them, Go into the village that is over against you, and straightway ye shall find an ass tied, and a colt with her: loose [them], and bring [them] unto me.
paragraphs.original: λέγων αὐτοῖς· Πορεύεσθε εἰς τὴν κώμην τὴν κατέναντι ὑμῶν, καὶ εὐθέως εὑρήσετε ὄνον δεδεμένην καὶ πῶλον μετʼ αὐτῆς· λύσαντες ἀγάγετέ μοι.
paragraphs.translit: legōn autois· Poreuesthe eis tēn kōmēn tēn katenanti hymōn, kai eutheōs heurēsete onon dedemenēn kai pōlon metʼ autēs· lysantes agagete moi.

paragraphs.text: And if any one say aught unto you, ye shall say, The Lord hath need of them; and straightway he will send them.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἐάν τις ὑμῖν εἴπῃ τι, ἐρεῖτε ὅτι Ὁ κύριος αὐτῶν χρείαν ἔχει· εὐθὺς δὲ ἀποστελεῖ αὐτούς.
paragraphs.translit: kai ean tis hymin eipē ti, ereite hoti Ho kyrios autōn chreian echei· euthys de apostelei autous.

paragraphs.text: Now this is come to pass, that it might be fulfilled which was spoken through the prophet, saying,
paragraphs.original: Τοῦτο δὲ γέγονεν ἵνα πληρωθῇ τὸ ῥηθὲν διὰ τοῦ προφήτου λέγοντος·
paragraphs.translit: Touto de gegonen hina plērōthē to rhēthen dia tou prophētou legontos·

paragraphs.text: Tell ye the daughter of Zion, Behold, thy King cometh unto thee, Meek, and riding upon an ass, And upon a colt the foal of an ass.
paragraphs.original: Εἴπατε τῇ θυγατρὶ Σιών· Ἰδοὺ ὁ βασιλεύς σου ἔρχεταί σοι πραῢς καὶ ἐπιβεβηκὼς ἐπὶ ὄνον καὶ ἐπὶ πῶλον υἱὸν ὑποζυγίου.
paragraphs.translit: Eipate tē thygatri Siōn· Idou ho basileus sou erchetai soi praus kai epibebēkōs epi onon kai epi pōlon hyion hypozygiou.

paragraphs.text: And the disciples went, and did even as Jesus appointed them,
paragraphs.original: πορευθέντες δὲ οἱ μαθηταὶ καὶ ποιήσαντες καθὼς συνέταξεν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς
paragraphs.translit: poreuthentes de hoi mathētai kai poiēsantes kathōs synetaxen autois ho Iēsous

paragraphs.text: and brought the ass, and the colt, and put on them their garments; and he sat thereon.
paragraphs.original: ἤγαγον τὴν ὄνον καὶ τὸν πῶλον, καὶ ἐπέθηκαν ἐπʼ αὐτῶν τὰ ἱμάτια, καὶ ἐπεκάθισεν ἐπάνω αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: ēgagon tēn onon kai ton pōlon, kai epethēkan epʼ autōn ta himatia, kai epekathisen epanō autōn.

paragraphs.text: And the most part of the multitude spread their garments in the way; and others cut branches from the trees, and spread them in the way.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ πλεῖστος ὄχλος ἔστρωσαν ἑαυτῶν τὰ ἱμάτια ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ, ἄλλοι δὲ ἔκοπτον κλάδους ἀπὸ τῶν δένδρων καὶ ἐστρώννυον ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ.
paragraphs.translit: ho de pleistos ochlos estrōsan heautōn ta himatia en tē hodō, alloi de ekopton kladous apo tōn dendrōn kai estrōnnyon en tē hodō.

paragraphs.text: And the multitudes that went before him, and that followed, cried, saying, Hosanna to the son of David: Blessed [is] he that cometh in the name of the Lord; Hosanna in the highest.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ ὄχλοι οἱ προάγοντες αὐτὸν καὶ οἱ ἀκολουθοῦντες ἔκραζον λέγοντες· Ὡσαννὰ τῷ υἱῷ Δαυίδ· Εὐλογημένος ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἐν ὀνόματι κυρίου· Ὡσαννὰ ἐν τοῖς ὑψίστοις.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de ochloi hoi proagontes auton kai hoi akolouthountes ekrazon legontes· Hōsanna tō hyiō Dauid· Eulogēmenos ho erchomenos en onomati kyriou· Hōsanna en tois hypsistois.

paragraphs.text: And when he was come into Jerusalem, all the city was stirred, saying, Who is this?
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἰσελθόντος αὐτοῦ εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα ἐσείσθη πᾶσα ἡ πόλις λέγουσα· Τίς ἐστιν οὗτος;
paragraphs.translit: kai eiselthontos autou eis Hierosolyma eseisthē pasa hē polis legousa· Tis estin houtos;

paragraphs.text: And the multitudes said, This is the prophet, Jesus, from Nazareth of Galilee.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ ὄχλοι ἔλεγον· Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ προφήτης Ἰησοῦς ὁ ἀπὸ Ναζαρὲθ τῆς Γαλιλαίας.
paragraphs.translit: hoi de ochloi elegon· Houtos estin ho prophētēs Iēsous ho apo Nazareth tēs Galilaias.

paragraphs.text: And Jesus entered into the temple of God, and cast out all them that sold and bought in the temple, and overthrew the tables of he money-changers, and the seats of them that sold the doves;
paragraphs.original: Καὶ εἰσῆλθεν Ἰησοῦς εἰς τὸ ἱερόν, καὶ ἐξέβαλεν πάντας τοὺς πωλοῦντας καὶ ἀγοράζοντας ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ καὶ τὰς τραπέζας τῶν κολλυβιστῶν κατέστρεψεν καὶ τὰς καθέδρας τῶν πωλούντων τὰς περιστεράς,
paragraphs.translit: Kai eisēlthen Iēsous eis to hieron, kai exebalen pantas tous pōlountas kai agorazontas en tō hierō kai tas trapezas tōn kollybistōn katestrepsen kai tas kathedras tōn pōlountōn tas peristeras,

paragraphs.text: and he saith unto them, It is written, My house shall be called a house of prayer: but ye make it a den of robbers.
paragraphs.original: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς· Γέγραπται· Ὁ οἶκός μου οἶκος προσευχῆς κληθήσεται, ὑμεῖς δὲ αὐτὸν ποιεῖτε σπήλαιον λῃστῶν.
paragraphs.translit: kai legei autois· Gegraptai· Ho oikos mou oikos proseuchēs klēthēsetai, hymeis de auton poieite spēlaion lēstōn.

paragraphs.text: And the blind and the lame came to him in the temple; and he healed them.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ προσῆλθον αὐτῷ τυφλοὶ καὶ χωλοὶ ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ, καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν αὐτούς.
paragraphs.translit: Kai prosēlthon autō typhloi kai chōloi en tō hierō, kai etherapeusen autous.

paragraphs.text: But when the chief priests and the scribes saw the wonderful things that he did, and the children that were crying in the temple and saying, Hosanna to the son of David; they were moved with indignation,
paragraphs.original: ἰδόντες δὲ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς τὰ θαυμάσια ἃ ἐποίησεν καὶ τοὺς παῖδας τοὺς κράζοντας ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ καὶ λέγοντας· Ὡσαννὰ τῷ υἱῷ Δαυίδ, ἠγανάκτησαν
paragraphs.translit: idontes de hoi archiereis kai hoi grammateis ta thaumasia ha epoiēsen kai tous paidas tous krazontas en tō hierō kai legontas· Hōsanna tō hyiō Dauid, ēganaktēsan

paragraphs.text: and said unto him, Hearest thou what these are saying? And Jesus saith unto them, Yea: did ye never read, Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings thou has perfected praise?
paragraphs.original: καὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ· Ἀκούεις τί οὗτοι λέγουσιν; ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς λέγει αὐτοῖς· Ναί. οὐδέποτε ἀνέγνωτε ὅτι Ἐκ στόματος νηπίων καὶ θηλαζόντων κατηρτίσω αἶνον;
paragraphs.translit: kai eipan autō· Akoueis ti houtoi legousin; ho de Iēsous legei autois· Nai. oudepote anegnōte hoti Ek stomatos nēpiōn kai thēlazontōn katērtisō ainon;

paragraphs.text: And he left them, and went forth out of the city to Bethany, and lodged there.
paragraphs.original: καὶ καταλιπὼν αὐτοὺς ἐξῆλθεν ἔξω τῆς πόλεως εἰς Βηθανίαν, καὶ ηὐλίσθη ἐκεῖ.
paragraphs.translit: kai katalipōn autous exēlthen exō tēs poleōs eis Bēthanian, kai ēulisthē ekei.

paragraphs.text: Now in the morning as he returned to the city, he hungered.
paragraphs.original: Πρωῒ δὲ ἐπανάγων εἰς τὴν πόλιν ἐπείνασεν.
paragraphs.translit: Prōi de epanagōn eis tēn polin epeinasen.

paragraphs.text: And seeing a fig tree by the way side, he came to it, and found nothing thereon, but leaves only; and he saith unto it, Let there be no fruit from thee henceforward for ever. And immediately the fig tree withered away.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἰδὼν συκῆν μίαν ἐπὶ τῆς ὁδοῦ ἦλθεν ἐπʼ αὐτήν, καὶ οὐδὲν εὗρεν ἐν αὐτῇ εἰ μὴ φύλλα μόνον, καὶ λέγει αὐτῇ· Μηκέτι ἐκ σοῦ καρπὸς γένηται εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα· καὶ ἐξηράνθη παραχρῆμα ἡ συκῆ.
paragraphs.translit: kai idōn sykēn mian epi tēs hodou ēlthen epʼ autēn, kai ouden heuren en autē ei mē phylla monon, kai legei autē· Mēketi ek sou karpos genētai eis ton aiōna· kai exēranthē parachrēma hē sykē.

paragraphs.text: And when the disciples saw it, they marvelled, saying, How did the fig tree immediately wither away?
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἰδόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ ἐθαύμασαν λέγοντες· Πῶς παραχρῆμα ἐξηράνθη ἡ συκῆ;
paragraphs.translit: kai idontes hoi mathētai ethaumasan legontes· Pōs parachrēma exēranthē hē sykē;

paragraphs.text: And Jesus answered and said unto them, Verily I say unto you, If ye have faith, and doubt not, ye shall not only do what is done to the fig tree, but even if ye shall say unto this mountain, Be thou taken up and cast into the sea, it shall be done.
paragraphs.original: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐὰν ἔχητε πίστιν καὶ μὴ διακριθῆτε, οὐ μόνον τὸ τῆς συκῆς ποιήσετε, ἀλλὰ κἂν τῷ ὄρει τούτῳ εἴπητε· Ἄρθητι καὶ βλήθητι εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν, γενήσεται·
paragraphs.translit: apokritheis de ho Iēsous eipen autois· Amēn legō hymin, ean echēte pistin kai mē diakrithēte, ou monon to tēs sykēs poiēsete, alla kan tō orei toutō eipēte· Arthēti kai blēthēti eis tēn thalassan, genēsetai·

paragraphs.text: And all things, whatsoever ye shall ask in prayer, believing, ye shall receive.
paragraphs.original: καὶ πάντα ὅσα ἂν αἰτήσητε ἐν τῇ προσευχῇ πιστεύοντες λήμψεσθε.
paragraphs.translit: kai panta hosa an aitēsēte en tē proseuchē pisteuontes lēmpsesthe.

paragraphs.text: And when he was come into the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people came unto him as he was teaching, and said, By what authority doest thou these things? and who gave thee this authority?
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἐλθόντος αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν προσῆλθον αὐτῷ διδάσκοντι οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι τοῦ λαοῦ λέγοντες· Ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιεῖς; καὶ τίς σοι ἔδωκεν τὴν ἐξουσίαν ταύτην;
paragraphs.translit: Kai elthontos autou eis to hieron prosēlthon autō didaskonti hoi archiereis kai hoi presbyteroi tou laou legontes· En poia exousia tauta poieis; kai tis soi edōken tēn exousian tautēn;

paragraphs.text: And Jesus answered and said unto them, I also will ask you one question, which if ye tell me, I likewise will tell you by what authority I do these things.
paragraphs.original: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ἐρωτήσω ὑμᾶς κἀγὼ λόγον ἕνα, ὃν ἐὰν εἴπητέ μοι κἀγὼ ὑμῖν ἐρῶ ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιῶ·
paragraphs.translit: apokritheis de ho Iēsous eipen autois· Erōtēsō hymas kagō logon hena, hon ean eipēte moi kagō hymin erō en poia exousia tauta poiō·

paragraphs.text: The baptism of John, whence was it? from heaven or from men? And they reasoned with themselves, saying, If we shall say, From heaven; he will say unto us, Why then did ye not believe him?
paragraphs.original: τὸ βάπτισμα τὸ Ἰωάννου πόθεν ἦν; ἐξ οὐρανοῦ ἢ ἐξ ἀνθρώπων; οἱ δὲ διελογίζοντο ἐν ἑαυτοῖς λέγοντες· Ἐὰν εἴπωμεν· Ἐξ οὐρανοῦ, ἐρεῖ ἡμῖν· Διὰ τί οὖν οὐκ ἐπιστεύσατε αὐτῷ;
paragraphs.translit: to baptisma to Iōannou pothen ēn; ex ouranou ē ex anthrōpōn; hoi de dielogizonto en heautois legontes· Ean eipōmen· Ex ouranou, erei hēmin· Dia ti oun ouk episteusate autō;

paragraphs.text: But if we shall say, From men; we fear the multitude; for all hold John as a prophet.
paragraphs.original: ἐὰν δὲ εἴπωμεν· Ἐξ ἀνθρώπων, φοβούμεθα τὸν ὄχλον, πάντες γὰρ ὡς προφήτην ἔχουσιν τὸν Ἰωάννην.
paragraphs.translit: ean de eipōmen· Ex anthrōpōn, phoboumetha ton ochlon, pantes gar hōs prophētēn echousin ton Iōannēn.

paragraphs.text: And they answered Jesus, and said, We know not. He also said unto them, Neither tell I you by what authority I do these things.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ἀποκριθέντες τῷ Ἰησοῦ εἶπαν· Οὐκ οἴδαμεν. ἔφη αὐτοῖς καὶ αὐτός· Οὐδὲ ἐγὼ λέγω ὑμῖν ἐν ποίᾳ ἐξουσίᾳ ταῦτα ποιῶ.
paragraphs.translit: kai apokrithentes tō Iēsou eipan· Ouk oidamen. ephē autois kai autos· Oude egō legō hymin en poia exousia tauta poiō.

paragraphs.text: But what think ye? A man had two sons; and he came to the first, and said, Son, go work to-day in the vineyard.
paragraphs.original: Τί δὲ ὑμῖν δοκεῖ; ἄνθρωπος εἶχεν τέκνα δύο. προσελθὼν τῷ πρώτῳ εἶπεν· Τέκνον, ὕπαγε σήμερον ἐργάζου ἐν τῷ ἀμπελῶνι.
paragraphs.translit: Ti de hymin dokei; anthrōpos eichen tekna dyo. proselthōn tō prōtō eipen· Teknon, hypage sēmeron ergazou en tō ampelōni.

paragraphs.text: And he answered and said, I will not: but afterward he repented himself, and went.
paragraphs.original: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Οὐ θέλω· ὕστερον δὲ μεταμεληθεὶς ἀπῆλθεν.
paragraphs.translit: ho de apokritheis eipen· Ou thelō· hysteron de metamelētheis apēlthen.

paragraphs.text: And he came to the second, and said likewise. And he answered and said, I [go], sir: and went not.
paragraphs.original: προσελθὼν δὲ τῷ δευτέρῳ εἶπεν ὡσαύτως· ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Ἐγώ, κύριε· καὶ οὐκ ἀπῆλθεν.
paragraphs.translit: proselthōn de tō deuterō eipen hōsautōs· ho de apokritheis eipen· Egō, kyrie· kai ouk apēlthen.

paragraphs.text: Which of the two did the will of his father? They say, The first. Jesus saith unto them, Verily I say unto you, that the publicans and the harlots go into the kingdom of God before you.
paragraphs.original: τίς ἐκ τῶν δύο ἐποίησεν τὸ θέλημα τοῦ πατρός; λέγουσιν· Ὁ πρῶτος. λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι οἱ τελῶναι καὶ αἱ πόρναι προάγουσιν ὑμᾶς εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ θεοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: tis ek tōn dyo epoiēsen to thelēma tou patros; legousin· Ho prōtos. legei autois ho Iēsous· Amēn legō hymin hoti hoi telōnai kai hai pornai proagousin hymas eis tēn basileian tou theou.

paragraphs.text: For John came unto you in the way of righteousness, and ye believed him not; but the publicans and the harlots believed him: and ye, when ye saw it, did not even repent yourselves afterward, that ye might believe him.
paragraphs.original: ἦλθεν γὰρ Ἰωάννης πρὸς ὑμᾶς ἐν ὁδῷ δικαιοσύνης, καὶ οὐκ ἐπιστεύσατε αὐτῷ· οἱ δὲ τελῶναι καὶ αἱ πόρναι ἐπίστευσαν αὐτῷ· ὑμεῖς δὲ ἰδόντες οὐδὲ μετεμελήθητε ὕστερον τοῦ πιστεῦσαι αὐτῷ.
paragraphs.translit: ēlthen gar Iōannēs pros hymas en hodō dikaiosynēs, kai ouk episteusate autō· hoi de telōnai kai hai pornai episteusan autō· hymeis de idontes oude metemelēthēte hysteron tou pisteusai autō.

paragraphs.text: Hear another parable: There was a man that was a householder, who planted a vineyard, and set a hedge about it, and digged a winepress in it, and built a tower, and let it out to husbandmen, and went into another country.
paragraphs.original: Ἄλλην παραβολὴν ἀκούσατε. Ἄνθρωπος ἦν οἰκοδεσπότης ὅστις ἐφύτευσεν ἀμπελῶνα καὶ φραγμὸν αὐτῷ περιέθηκεν καὶ ὤρυξεν ἐν αὐτῷ ληνὸν καὶ ᾠκοδόμησεν πύργον, καὶ ἐξέδετο αὐτὸν γεωργοῖς, καὶ ἀπεδήμησεν.
paragraphs.translit: Allēn parabolēn akousate. Anthrōpos ēn oikodespotēs hostis ephyteusen ampelōna kai phragmon autō periethēken kai ōryxen en autō lēnon kai ōkodomēsen pyrgon, kai exedeto auton geōrgois, kai apedēmēsen.

paragraphs.text: And when the season of the fruits drew near, he sent his servants to the husbandmen, to receive his fruits.
paragraphs.original: ὅτε δὲ ἤγγισεν ὁ καιρὸς τῶν καρπῶν, ἀπέστειλεν τοὺς δούλους αὐτοῦ πρὸς τοὺς γεωργοὺς λαβεῖν τοὺς καρποὺς αὐτοῦ.
paragraphs.translit: hote de ēngisen ho kairos tōn karpōn, apesteilen tous doulous autou pros tous geōrgous labein tous karpous autou.

paragraphs.text: And the husbandmen took his servants, and beat one, and killed another, and stoned another.
paragraphs.original: καὶ λαβόντες οἱ γεωργοὶ τοὺς δούλους αὐτοῦ ὃν μὲν ἔδειραν, ὃν δὲ ἀπέκτειναν, ὃν δὲ ἐλιθοβόλησαν.
paragraphs.translit: kai labontes hoi geōrgoi tous doulous autou hon men edeiran, hon de apekteinan, hon de elithobolēsan.

paragraphs.text: Again, he sent other servants more than the first: and they did unto them in like manner.
paragraphs.original: πάλιν ἀπέστειλεν ἄλλους δούλους πλείονας τῶν πρώτων, καὶ ἐποίησαν αὐτοῖς ὡσαύτως.
paragraphs.translit: palin apesteilen allous doulous pleionas tōn prōtōn, kai epoiēsan autois hōsautōs.

paragraphs.text: But afterward he sent unto them his son, saying, They will reverence my son.
paragraphs.original: ὕστερον δὲ ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς αὐτοὺς τὸν υἱὸν αὐτοῦ λέγων· Ἐντραπήσονται τὸν υἱόν μου.
paragraphs.translit: hysteron de apesteilen pros autous ton hyion autou legōn· Entrapēsontai ton hyion mou.

paragraphs.text: But the husbandmen, when they saw the son, said among themselves, This is the heir; come, let us kill him, and take his inheritance.
paragraphs.original: οἱ δὲ γεωργοὶ ἰδόντες τὸν υἱὸν εἶπον ἐν ἑαυτοῖς· Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ κληρονόμος· δεῦτε ἀποκτείνωμεν αὐτὸν καὶ σχῶμεν τὴν κληρονομίαν αὐτοῦ·
paragraphs.translit: hoi de geōrgoi idontes ton hyion eipon en heautois· Houtos estin ho klēronomos· deute apokteinōmen auton kai schōmen tēn klēronomian autou·

paragraphs.text: And they took him, and cast him forth out of the vineyard, and killed him.
paragraphs.original: καὶ λαβόντες αὐτὸν ἐξέβαλον ἔξω τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος καὶ ἀπέκτειναν.
paragraphs.translit: kai labontes auton exebalon exō tou ampelōnos kai apekteinan.

paragraphs.text: When therefore the lord of the vineyard shall come, what will he do unto those husbandmen?
paragraphs.original: ὅταν οὖν ἔλθῃ ὁ κύριος τοῦ ἀμπελῶνος, τί ποιήσει τοῖς γεωργοῖς ἐκείνοις;
paragraphs.translit: hotan oun elthē ho kyrios tou ampelōnos, ti poiēsei tois geōrgois ekeinois;

paragraphs.text: They say unto him, He will miserably destroy those miserable men, and will let out the vineyard unto other husbandmen, who shall render him the fruits in their seasons.
paragraphs.original: λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Κακοὺς κακῶς ἀπολέσει αὐτούς, καὶ τὸν ἀμπελῶνα ἐκδώσεται ἄλλοις γεωργοῖς, οἵτινες ἀποδώσουσιν αὐτῷ τοὺς καρποὺς ἐν τοῖς καιροῖς αὐτῶν.
paragraphs.translit: legousin autō· Kakous kakōs apolesei autous, kai ton ampelōna ekdōsetai allois geōrgois, hoitines apodōsousin autō tous karpous en tois kairois autōn.

paragraphs.text: Jesus saith unto them, Did ye never read in the scriptures, The stone which the builders rejected, The same was made the head of the corner; This was from the Lord, And it is marvelous in our eyes?
paragraphs.original: Λέγει αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Οὐδέποτε ἀνέγνωτε ἐν ταῖς γραφαῖς· Λίθον ὃν ἀπεδοκίμασαν οἱ οἰκοδομοῦντες οὗτος ἐγενήθη εἰς κεφαλὴν γωνίας· παρὰ κυρίου ἐγένετο αὕτη, καὶ ἔστιν θαυμαστὴ ἐν ὀφθαλμοῖς ἡμῶν;
paragraphs.translit: Legei autois ho Iēsous· Oudepote anegnōte en tais graphais· Lithon hon apedokimasan hoi oikodomountes houtos egenēthē eis kephalēn gōnias· para kyriou egeneto hautē, kai estin thaumastē en ophthalmois hēmōn;

paragraphs.text: Therefore say I unto you, The kingdom of God shall be taken away from you, and shall be given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof.
paragraphs.original: διὰ τοῦτο λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι ἀρθήσεται ἀφʼ ὑμῶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ δοθήσεται ἔθνει ποιοῦντι τοὺς καρποὺς αὐτῆς.
paragraphs.translit: dia touto legō hymin hoti arthēsetai aphʼ hymōn hē basileia tou theou kai dothēsetai ethnei poiounti tous karpous autēs.

paragraphs.text: And he that falleth on this stone shall be broken to pieces: but on whomsoever it shall fall, it will scatter him as dust.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ὁ πεσὼν ἐπὶ τὸν λίθον τοῦτον συνθλασθήσεται· ἐφʼ ὃν δʼ ἂν πέσῃ λικμήσει αὐτόν.
paragraphs.translit: Kai ho pesōn epi ton lithon touton synthlasthēsetai· ephʼ hon dʼ an pesē likmēsei auton.

paragraphs.text: And when the chief priests and the Pharisees heard his parables, they perceived that he spake of them.
paragraphs.original: Καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι τὰς παραβολὰς αὐτοῦ ἔγνωσαν ὅτι περὶ αὐτῶν λέγει·
paragraphs.translit: Kai akousantes hoi archiereis kai hoi Pharisaioi tas parabolas autou egnōsan hoti peri autōn legei·

paragraphs.text: And when they sought to lay hold on him, they feared the multitudes, because they took him for a prophet.
paragraphs.original: καὶ ζητοῦντες αὐτὸν κρατῆσαι ἐφοβήθησαν τοὺς ὄχλους, ἐπεὶ εἰς προφήτην αὐτὸν εἶχον.
paragraphs.translit: kai zētountes auton kratēsai ephobēthēsan tous ochlous, epei eis prophētēn auton eichon.
